title.en: What Kind of Magic Shopkeeper Would You Be?
title.zh: 如果开一家魔法小店，你是哪种店主？

description.en: Six original magical-shop scenes find your shopkeeper portrait: the careful labeler, the lending librarian, or the small-wonder demonstrator. Every result is free.
description.zh: 6个原创魔法小店情境，看看你是认真贴标签的店主、愿意借出魔法的馆员，还是演示小奇迹的人。完整结果免费。

introduction.en: Your shop sells harmless imaginary things: umbrellas that remember sunshine and jars that hold an echo. There is no business score. Choose the kind of welcome and explanation you would enjoy offering, within a completely fictional setting.
introduction.zh: 你的小店只有无害的想象物品：记得阳光的伞、装得下一声回响的瓶子。这里没有经营评分，请在完全虚构的场景里，选择你愿意提供的欢迎与说明方式。

focus.en: How you make an unfamiliar magical object understandable, borrowable, or enjoyable to discover.
focus.zh: 你怎样让一件陌生的魔法物品变得好理解、方便借用，或值得发现。

prompt.en: A visitor asks what a “yesterday jar” does. You…
prompt.zh: 客人问“昨日瓶”是做什么的，你会……

label.en: Point to a clear label showing what it can and cannot hold.
label.zh: 指给对方看清楚的标签：能装什么，不能装什么。

label.en: Offer a short loan so they can see whether it suits their story.
label.zh: 借出一小段时间，让对方看看是否适合自己的故事。

label.en: Demonstrate one tiny echo, then let them ask questions.
label.zh: 演示一声小小的回响，再让对方提问。

prompt.en: Someone needs a sunshine umbrella for just one evening. You prefer to…
prompt.zh: 有人只想在一个晚上用一下阳光伞，你更愿意……

label.en: Arrange a simple return time and lend it.
label.zh: 约好简单的归还时间，再借出去。

label.en: Show its effect before they decide what to do.
label.zh: 先展示效果，再让对方决定。

label.en: Explain exactly how long its stored sunshine lasts.
label.zh: 说明它储存的阳光究竟能持续多久。

prompt.en: A new item arrives with an unclear instruction card. You…
prompt.zh: 新到的小物件，说明卡却写得含糊，你会……

label.en: Keep it off display until its limits are clear enough to describe.
label.zh: 先不摆出来，等能说明它的边界。

label.en: Try a small harmless demonstration in the shop’s test corner.
label.zh: 在店里的试用角做一次无害的小演示。

label.en: Ask whether it belongs in the supervised borrowing collection first.
label.zh: 看看能否先放进有陪同说明的借用区。

prompt.en: A customer returns an item because it was not what they imagined. You…
prompt.zh: 客人还回物品，说它和想象的不一样，你会……

label.en: Ask what a short trial could help them understand next time.
label.zh: 问问下次怎样的短期试用会更有帮助。

label.en: Look at which part of the label set the wrong expectation.
label.zh: 看看标签哪一处让人产生了不同预期。

label.en: Invite them to a brief demonstration of another small wonder, if they want.
label.zh: 如果对方愿意，邀请再看一个小奇迹的演示。

prompt.zh: 你最喜欢的小店陈列会是……

label.en: A little demonstration that changes when a visitor asks a question.
label.zh: 一个会随着客人提问而变化的小演示。

label.en: A shelf of clearly marked objects, each with one honest promise.
label.zh: 一架标示清楚、每件只有一项诚实承诺的物品。

label.en: A traveling collection with notes from previous borrowers.
label.zh: 一组可以流转、留着借用者小记的收藏。

prompt.en: What would make closing time feel satisfying?
prompt.zh: 打烊时，什么会让你满意？

label.en: Someone understood a strange object without being oversold a miracle.
label.zh: 有人理解了陌生物件，没有被夸大的奇迹吸引。

label.en: An object began another temporary journey and has a way home.
label.zh: 一件物品又踏上短暂旅程，也约好了回家的方式。

label.en: A visitor left delighted by one small unexpected thing.
label.zh: 有位客人因为一个小意外，开心地离开。

summary.en: Your imaginary shop makes wonder easier to approach through clear expectations. You want visitors to know what an object actually does before they build a story around it. In this portrait, a limit is part of the object’s charm rather than something to hide.
summary.zh: 你的想象小店通过清楚的预期，让奇妙更容易靠近。你希望客人先知道物品实际能做什么，再围绕它展开想象。在这份画像里，边界也是魅力的一部分，不需要藏起来。

example.en: Your sunshine umbrella might carry a note saying it remembers one afternoon, not an entire summer. In everyday life, the playful parallel is explaining what a shared tool is good for before lending it.
example.zh: 你的阳光伞上可能写着：能记住一个下午，不是一整个夏天。放在日常，类似的小做法是先说明共用工具擅长什么，再借给别人。

strength.en: You can turn unfamiliar possibilities into understandable choices and leave less room for disappointment caused by a vague or oversized promise.
strength.zh: 你能把陌生的可能性变成容易理解的选择，也减少因为承诺模糊或过大而产生的失望。

tradeoff.en: Too much explanation can bury the enjoyable first encounter. A visitor may need one clear sentence now and the rest only when they ask.
tradeoff.zh: 解释太多，也可能盖住第一次接触的乐趣。客人现在也许只需要一句清楚的话，其余部分可以等提问时再说。

experiment.en: For one ordinary thing you share this week, try stating its most useful feature and one real limit. Then leave room for the other person’s curiosity.
experiment.zh: 这周分享一件普通东西时，可以试着说清最有用的一点，以及一个真实边界。然后给对方自己的好奇留空间。

summary.en: You imagine a shop where an object does not have to belong to someone forever to matter. A small loan lets a visitor explore and lets the collection keep moving. Your portrait values access, return, and stories that accumulate through shared use.
summary.zh: 你想象的小店里，物品不必永远属于一个人，才有意义。一段小借期让客人探索，也让收藏继续流动。你的画像重视能够接触、方便归还，以及在共同使用里积累的故事。

example.en: A jar of echoes might spend an evening at a quiet gathering, then return with a short note about its journey. The everyday analogy is sharing a hobby kit with clear expectations.
example.zh: 回响瓶可以在一场安静聚会里待一晚，再带着一小段旅程记录回来。日常里的类似做法，是在预期清楚的前提下分享一组爱好工具。

strength.en: You can create a low-pressure way to try something without turning curiosity into permanent ownership. A return path helps sharing feel manageable.
strength.zh: 你能让尝试新东西不必立刻变成长期拥有。归还方式清楚，也让分享更容易管理。

tradeoff.en: Generosity still needs boundaries around time, care, and availability. An imaginary endless lending shelf would eventually ask too much of its keeper.
tradeoff.zh: 慷慨同样需要时间、照顾与可用性的边界。哪怕是想象中的无限借阅架，也会逐渐让管理者负担过多。

experiment.en: If you choose to lend an ordinary item, agree on one clear return arrangement and what care it needs. Let yourself decline a loan that would feel uncomfortable.
experiment.zh: 如果决定借出一件普通物品，可以约好一个明确的归还安排，并说明需要怎样照顾。让自己也能够拒绝不舒服的借用请求。

summary.en: Your magical shop invites curiosity through a concrete little experience. Rather than explain everything first, you offer one harmless surprise that people can see and ask about. The delight is in opening a question, not claiming a spectacle can solve every problem.
summary.zh: 你的魔法小店通过一个具体的小体验邀请好奇。不急着先解释全部，而是提供一个无害、看得见、问得着的小惊喜。乐趣在于打开问题，不声称一场奇观能解决所有问题。

example.en: You might let an echo jar repeat a visitor’s laugh once, then explain its modest limits. Outside the story, you may enjoy showing a tiny prototype before describing an entire idea.
example.zh: 你可能让回响瓶只重复一次客人的笑声，再说明它有限的能力。走出故事，你也许会喜欢先展示一个小试样，再讲完整想法。

strength.en: You make unfamiliar ideas approachable and can give people a memorable place to begin. A small demonstration may invite questions that a long description would not.
strength.zh: 你让陌生想法更容易接近，也给人一个记得住的起点。小演示可能引出长篇说明不容易带来的问题。

tradeoff.en: A charming demonstration can make an object seem more useful than it is. Visitors still need a chance to understand its limits and decide against it.
tradeoff.zh: 有魅力的演示，也可能让物品显得比实际更有用。客人仍然需要理解边界，并保留不选择它的机会。

experiment.en: Show one small example when sharing a hobby idea, then name what the example does not establish. Invite someone to try it only if they are interested.
experiment.zh: 分享一个爱好想法时，可以演示一个小例子，再说清它不能证明什么。只有对方感兴趣时，再邀请一起试试。
